description: Inspired by two well-known ways periodic artefacts hide in sensor data: 50/60 Hz mains hum picked up by instruments, and 'hunting', where a badly tuned chiller or HVAC control loop keeps oscillating around its set-point. Rack R04's inlet temperature carries a sine wave with a 3-hour period (every 6 readings). Its random noise was reduced so that its mean, spread and histogram match the other racks. All six racks also share a genuine daily workload cycle as a decoy. Sort each rack by time and take a periodogram (np.fft.rfft) or autocorrelation, or average the readings by position in a 6-reading cycle. R04 alone shows a spike at 8 cycles per day, about 100 times the median of its spectrum.
hints: Means, spreads and histograms look the same for every rack. Stop looking at the values themselves and look at their order in time, one rack at a time.

Sort each rack's inlet_temp_c by timestamp, then compute a periodogram (np.fft.rfft) or the autocorrelation at several lags. Every rack shares a daily rhythm, so look for a peak that only one rack has.
Rack R04's inlet temperature oscillates with a 3-hour period (every 6 readings). Its spectrum has a spike at 8 cycles per day that no other rack has. R04's chiller is hunting.
